Definition: from G5259 and a derivative of G473; to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), i.e. to encounter, fall in with:--(go to) meet.
BiblicalUsage: hypantáō means to meet, to go to meet. In Matthew 8:28, the text says "there met him two possessed with devils." In Mark 5:2, the text says "immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit."
TheologicalSignificance: hypantáō convinces me that fellowship is sharing life together under Christ, not just sharing a room. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Heals the Gerasene Demoniac; The Healing of the Official's Son
